Girls' Pastimes in Japan.
O Hina Sama.—Dolls to represent the Emperor and Empress.
On the veranda, sits Umeko San (Miss Plum,) a young girl of good family.
Haruko San (Miss Spring) is dressing her sister's hair.
The children next door are donning their best attire.
At the gate, Yoshiko San receives her friends.
On arrival at the entrance to the house, the visitors are welcomed with profound bows by Yoshiko San's sisters.
In the drawing-room, Yoshiko San and her sisters serve the guests with tea.
The attraction of the day is the display of dolls and their miniature house furnishings.
In a large room over-looking the garden, three of the visitors entertain the company with music.
Dear little Okiku San (Miss Chrysanthemum,) the youngest, and pet of all, now gives her prettiest dance.
Games follow. The first is throwing a fan at the gay toy on top of the box.
In groups, the girls play on the veranda.
See how skillfully the girls send the bean-bags high up into the air.
Before dinner, the girls wash their hands.
Dinner.
After dinner,—a walk in the garden.
Battledoor and shuttlecock.
Blind man's buff.
Swiftly round and round goes the water-wheel in the Yodo river.
A game of tag.
The last child is to be caught by the girl who is alone.
Skipping rope when one wears sandals on the feet requires care and skill.
It is such fun to play "house" and to do cooking on the veranda.
Afternoon tea in the garden.
The end of a happy day.
Published by The Tamamura, Photographic Studio & Art Gallery, Kobe. (Kolophon)
